_readme: The list of event calendars the importer reads. Adding a source is a one-line
pull request — see tools/README.md for the fields and how to test one.
Nothing in here is scraped against a site's wishes. Every entry is either a feed
the organisation publishes on purpose (ICS, RSS, a REST API) or structured data
they embed for machines to read. Sources with enabled:false are ones we have not
got permission or a working feed for yet; the note says what is needed.
ics     an iCalendar feed (.ics). The most reliable kind.
rss     an RSS or Atom feed.
tribe   WordPress 'The Events Calendar' REST API.
jsonld  schema.org Event markup embedded in a normal web page.
dateFrom: 'feed' (default) reads the real event date from the feed.
'content' hunts for a date in the title and description. Use only for
RSS feeds that publish a post date rather than an event date, and

sources.name: Township of Uxbridge
sources.note: Loop municipal CMS. Publishes a real subscribe-to-calendar ICS feed.

sources.name: Scugog Council for the Arts
sources.note: WordPress + Modern Events Calendar. The feed carries post dates, so event dates are read out of the text.

sources.name: Brock Township Public Library
sources.note: WordPress + The Events Calendar. Endpoint works; calendar was empty when last checked.

sources.name: OnStage Uxbridge
sources.note: Uxbridge Music Hall programming. WordPress + The Events Calendar.

sources.name: Uxbridge Public Library
sources.note: Insignia ILS feed. Was returning stale 2022 items when last checked — ask the library whether it is configured correctly.

sources.name: Sideroads of Scugog
sources.note: Squarespace. If the events page is a real Squarespace Events collection, ?format=rss works — open that URL in a browser to check, then set enabled:true. Could not be verified automatically.

sources.name: Uxbridge Historical Centre
sources.note: Embedded Google Calendar. The ICS works only if the calendar is shared publicly. Open the URL in a browser; if it downloads a file, set enabled:true.

sources.name: Royal Canadian Legion Branch 170, Uxbridge
sources.note: Probably Squarespace, same check as Sideroads.

sources.name: Township of Scugog
sources.note: NEEDS A FEED. Runs on Govstack, which offers email subscriptions only. This is the most valuable missing source — the main calendar for Port Perry, Blackstock and Caesarea. See tools/feed-request-letter.md.

sources.name: Township of Brock
sources.note: NEEDS A FEED. Govstack, email subscriptions only. Covers Beaverton, Cannington and Sunderland.

sources.name: Durham Region
sources.note: NEEDS A FEED. Govstack. Already aggregates North Durham events, so one feed here would cover many organisations at once.

sources.name: North Durham Chamber of Commerce
sources.note: NEEDS A FEED. Runs GrowthZone, which can publish feeds — this is likely just a setting for them to switch on. Well-populated calendar, worth asking.

sources.name: Scugog Memorial Public Library
sources.note: NEEDS A FEED. Full programme calendar published as a monthly PDF; the site blocks automated access.

sources.name: Town Hall 1873
sources.note: NEEDS A FEED. Busy theatre, calendar rendered by JavaScript, ticketing through Arts People which may offer an export.

sources.name: durhamregion.com events
sources.note: DO NOT SCRAPE. Metroland/Torstar, commercially licensed content, and the site blocks automated access. Written permission would be needed before importing anything from here.

sources.name: The Uxbridge Cosmos
sources.note: ASK THEM. The best aggregator in Uxbridge — it already carries the Studio Tour, the Fall Fair, the Historical Centre, the horticultural society and guided trail walks. But their Squarespace RSS publishes the date each entry was POSTED, not the date of the event, so importing it would put everything on the wrong day. The dates do exist at ?format=json, and Squarespace's robots.txt explicitly disallows that URL, so we do not use it. Worth emailing to ask whether they would share their listings another way.

sources.name: Lake Simcoe Region Conservation Authority
sources.note: WordPress + EventON. The watershed reaches Barrie and Newmarket, so this is filtered to North Durham. Carries Brock tree plantings and Cannington horticultural events.

sources.name: Oak Ridges Trail Association
sources.note: Wild Apricot. Guided hikes along the whole moraine, so filtered to ours — Uxbridge is the Trail Capital of Canada and gets a good share.

sources.name: Ontario Conservation Areas
sources.note: Province-wide, so heavily filtered. Endpoint is live but was returning zero upcoming events when added — that is an empty calendar, not a broken feed.

sources.name: Discover Uxbridge
sources.note: BLOCKED. The feed URL now returns a SiteGround bot-protection captcha page (HTTP 202 with an sgcaptcha redirect) rather than RSS. It parsed once, so the block may be new or intermittent. Their calendar content was a year stale anyway. Leave off unless they confirm they are happy for us to read it.

sources.name: Artists of Uxbridge
sources.note: NEEDS A FEED. Very active — shows, AGM, monthly figure-drawing workshops — but every event is hand-typed. They already run WordPress, so an events plugin would give them a feed for free.

sources.name: Town Hall 1873 (feed switched off)
sources.note: HIGHEST-LEVERAGE ASK. They already have The Events Calendar installed, but its REST and iCal outputs are switched off. For their webmaster this is a settings checkbox, not a project.

sources.name: Blue Heron Books
sources.note: Many author events plus the Book Drunkard Festival. The page is drawn by JavaScript so no feed could be confirmed — open it in a browser and view source before emailing them.

sources.name: Lake Scugog Historical Society
sources.note: The feed URL returns valid RSS with zero items, and their plain blog feed is also empty, so it is unclear whether the plugin is installed. Three real 2026 events sit on the page. Re-test before emailing.

sources.name: Beaverton Town Hall Players
sources.note: Full 2026 season, blog only, no feed tags. They sell through Eventbrite, which may be an easier route to ask about than their website.

sources.name: Ontario Nature
sources.note: Runs The Events Calendar with REST and iCal returning 404 while the HTML renders — deliberately switched off. Carries Durham Region Field Naturalists listings. Worth one polite ask.

sources.name: North Durham Nature
sources.note: DORMANT — do not revisit. Newest content on the site is from June 2017. Any current activity is on Facebook only, which has no public events API.

sources.name: Uxbridge Studio Tour
sources.note: Runs on Tymbrel, which publishes nothing machine-readable. No need to chase it: The Uxbridge Cosmos feed already carries the tour.
